verdict: Dictionary and gallery implemented and checked; no complete planet or canopy match claimed.

P01.reason: 203 unique imported parts; native gallery reads the same mesh dictionary used for future assembly.

P02.reason: Literal part bounds and visible pane silhouettes checked. Complete assembled-planet silhouettes remain untested.

P03.reason: All 160 pane entries have expected bounds; all 16 lime states inspected together, plus individual side/underside views.

P04.reason: Full glass and panes shown together; native pixel tests verify clear/tinted alpha, opaque occlusion and order independence.

P05.reason: Meshes, original texture alpha and catalogued emission remain independent; nearby receiver light test passes.

P06.reason: Ten glass colours are available and inspected. Colour placement to break a complete planet silhouette has not been implemented or tested.

P07.reason: Native texture bytes/alpha match their archive sources; all 16 cores and reference cube inspected at block scale.

P08.reason: Gallery controls and label selection implemented; hidden native views cover overview, individual, side and underside. Human mouse interaction has not been manually exercised.

P09.reason: Separate gallery renderer and local settings; FSTAR layouts and accepted Python lighting code unchanged. All ten regression groups passed.

P10.reason: 1.19.3 source and static-texture/no-shadow limitations documented. This is a parts library, with no claimed planet/canopy match.

D01.reason: Historical canopy criterion; this separate parts-only gallery does not regenerate, evaluate or promote a star/scaffold candidate.

limitations: Original assets are from installed Minecraft 1.19.3, not a recovered reference version.
Animated textures use the first frame. No shadows, ambient occlusion or bloom.
Transparent face ordering is validated for separated gallery parts, not arbitrary intersecting assembled meshes.
Adjacent-part face suppression and automatic connection selection belong to future assembly.
Complete planet shapes, ring proportions and colour-based silhouette breakup remain untested.
